outcome: Hospital discharge rates for congenital viral infections
Association between congenital viral infections and perinatal and maternal factors
cohort: Infants born in England between 1968 and 2016
finding: Hospital discharge rates for congenital cytomegalovirus, HSV, and VZV increased from 1968 to 2016, likely due to improved diagnostics and screening, while rates for congenital rubella decreased, likely due to the MMR vaccine.
mod_finding: Congenital cytomegalovirus infection was associated with Cesarean section delivery, while congenital HSV infection was associated with vaginal and emergency Cesarean section deliveries.
